title.narrative: Emergency GBV Support for Displaced Women and Girls in Lebanon

description.narrative: The recent conflict between Israel and Hizbollah has displaced approximately 1 million individuals across Lebanon, forcing many into informal settlements, collective shelters, and host communities. This crisis has compounded Lebanon’s ongoing economic and social challenges, leaving over 80% of the population in poverty. Women and girls of reproductive age, who make up 36% of the displaced, face heightened vulnerabilities, especially regarding their hygiene and safety. The lack of basic sanitary supplies not only increases the risk of reproductive health infections but also exposes them to greater risks of gender-based violence (GBV).As of October 1, 2024, IOM DTM reports that 142,361 internally displaced persons (IDPs) are living in collective shelters, including approximately 40,000 women and girls of reproductive age. To address these urgent needs, UNFPA Lebanon will implement a six-month, $1 million project focused on comprehensive GBV prevention and response services. The project will distribute 60,000 dignity kits tailored to the cultural and practical needs of women and girls. These kits not only provide essential hygiene items but also serve as a critical entry point for sharing information and services.During distributions, UNFPA will engage women and girls through participatory discussions to better understand their needs, share details on available support services, and provide information on where to seek help. In collaboration with partners, UNFPA will deliver lifesaving GBV interventions, including Psychological First Aid (PFA), safe identification and referral, and comprehensive case management for GBV survivors, including cash assistance. Safety audits will also be conducted to identify protection issues and ensure safe spaces.As the provider of last resort for the GBV Working Group, UNFPA will leverage its extensive experience in GBV programming and dignity kit distribution to safeguard the health, dignity, and safety of displaced women and girls in Lebanon. Under the National Protection Sector, UNFPA co-chairs the Gender-Based Violence Working Group (GBV-WG), along with the Ministry of Social Affairs and UNHCR. It includes all GBV actors in Lebanon, and aims to ensure effective GBV prevention, response, and risk mitigation programmes. UNFPA, through coordinated efforts, is stepping up as a Provider Last Resort for the current emergency response, enhancing its coordination role to provide support to over one million displaced persons.
